questions.stem: Explain the following accounting concepts and conventions, giving an example of how each is applied: (a) going concern; (b) consistency; (c) money measurement; (d) dual aspect; (e) materiality. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: going concern: the business is assumed to continue in the foreseeable future, so assets are shown at cost less depreciation, not forced-sale value
2 marks: consistency: the same accounting methods are used from year to year, e.g. same depreciation method
2 marks: money measurement: only items measurable in money are recorded, e.g. staff morale is not recorded
2 marks: dual aspect: every transaction has two equal effects, e.g. assets = capital + liabilities
2 marks: materiality: insignificant items may be treated simply, e.g. a cheap stapler written off as an expense
questions.explanation: Going concern values assets on the basis that the business continues. Consistency requires the same methods each year so results are comparable. Money measurement records only items with a money value. Dual aspect underlies double entry: each transaction affects two accounts and the accounting equation. Materiality allows small items to be treated in the simplest way.

questions.stem:

(b) Explain, with an example of each, four errors that do not affect the agreement of the trial balance. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: to check the arithmetical accuracy of double-entry postings
1 mark: to provide a summary of balances for preparing final accounts
2 marks: error of omission: a transaction completely left out, e.g. an invoice not recorded at all
2 marks: error of commission: posting to the wrong personal account of the correct class, e.g. Ade's payment credited to Ada
2 marks: error of principle: posting to the wrong class of account, e.g. purchase of a van debited to purchases
2 marks: error of original entry / complete reversal / compensating error with a correct example
questions.explanation: A trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy and summarises balances for final accounts. Errors that leave it in balance include omission, commission, principle, original entry, complete reversal of entries and compensating errors, because equal debits and credits are still recorded.

questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: the reduction in the value of a non-current asset over its useful life
1 mark: wear and tear through use
1 mark: passage of time
1 mark: obsolescence / depletion
1 mark: (2,400,000 - 400,000) / 5 shown
2 marks: annual depreciation N400,000
2 marks: NBV after 3 years = 2,400,000 - 1,200,000 = N1,200,000
questions.explanation: Depreciation is the fall in value of a non-current asset caused by wear and tear, time, obsolescence or depletion. Straight-line: (2,400,000 - 400,000) / 5 = 400,000 a year; after 3 years accumulated depreciation is 1,200,000, leaving a net book value of 1,200,000.

questions.stem:
The following balances were extracted from the books of Okon Stores for the year ended 31 December: Sales N1,250,000; Purchases N780,000; Stock (1 January) N95,000; Returns inwards N20,000; Returns outwards N15,000; Carriage inwards N12,000; Salaries N140,000; Rent N60,000; Electricity N24,000; Discount received N8,000.
Additional information: (i) stock at 31 December, N110,000; (ii) rent prepaid, N10,000; (iii) salaries owing, N15,000.
(a) Prepare the trading account, showing cost of goods sold and gross profit. [10 marks]
(b) Prepare the profit and loss account, showing net profit. [8 marks]
(c) State how the rent prepaid and salaries owing will appear in the balance sheet. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: net sales 1,250,000 - 20,000 = 1,230,000
2 marks: net purchases 780,000 - 15,000 = 765,000
1 mark: carriage inwards 12,000 added
1 mark: opening stock 95,000 added
2 marks: cost of goods sold 762,000 after deducting closing stock 110,000
2 marks: gross profit N468,000
1 mark: discount received 8,000 added to gross profit
2 marks: salaries 140,000 + 15,000 = 155,000
2 marks: rent 60,000 - 10,000 = 50,000 and electricity 24,000 (total expenses 229,000)
3 marks: net profit N247,000
1 mark: rent prepaid shown as a current asset
1 mark: salaries owing shown as a current liability
questions.explanation: Net sales 1,230,000. Cost of goods sold = 95,000 + (765,000 + 12,000) - 110,000 = 762,000. Gross profit = 468,000. Add discount received 8,000 = 476,000; less salaries 155,000, rent 50,000, electricity 24,000 (229,000). Net profit = 247,000. Rent prepaid is a current asset; salaries owing is a current liability.

Purchases ledger: creditors 1 June N132,000; credit purchases N640,000; cheques paid to creditors N585,000; discount received N9,800; returns outwards N11,200; set-off N9,000.
(a) Prepare the sales ledger control account. [10 marks]
(b) Prepare the purchases ledger control account. [8 marks]
(c) State two uses of control accounts. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: opening debtors 184,000 debited
1 mark: credit sales 960,000 debited
1 mark: dishonoured cheque 7,500 debited
1 mark: receipts 812,000 credited
1 mark: discount allowed 14,500 credited
1 mark: returns inwards 21,000 credited
1 mark: bad debts 6,000 credited
1 mark: set-off 9,000 credited
2 marks: closing debtors N289,000
1 mark: opening creditors 132,000 credited
1 mark: credit purchases 640,000 credited
1 mark: payments 585,000 debited
1 mark: discount received 9,800 debited
1 mark: returns outwards 11,200 debited

Purchases ledger control: 132,000 + 640,000 - (585,000 + 9,800 + 11,200 + 9,000) = 157,000 credit. Control accounts check ledger accuracy, localise errors, give quick totals and help prevent fraud.

questions.stem:
Ibeto Manufacturing Company provides the following for the year: raw materials 1 January N65,000; purchases of raw materials N540,000; carriage on raw materials N15,000; raw materials 31 December N80,000; direct wages N310,000; direct expenses N45,000; indirect wages N72,000; factory rent N48,000; factory power N36,000; depreciation of plant N30,000; work in progress 1 January N28,000; work in progress 31 December N34,000. 25,000 units were produced.
(a) Calculate the cost of raw materials consumed. [5 marks]
(b) Calculate the prime cost. [4 marks]
(c) Calculate the total factory overheads. [5 marks]
(d) Calculate the cost of production. [4 marks]
(e) Calculate the cost per unit produced. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: 65,000 + 540,000 + 15,000 - 80,000 shown
2 marks: raw materials consumed N540,000
2 marks: 540,000 + 310,000 + 45,000 shown
2 marks: prime cost N895,000
3 marks: 72,000 + 48,000 + 36,000 + 30,000 shown
2 marks: factory overheads N186,000
2 marks: 895,000 + 186,000 + 28,000 - 34,000 shown
2 marks: cost of production N1,075,000
2 marks: N1,075,000 / 25,000 = N43 per unit
questions.explanation: Raw materials consumed = 65,000 + 540,000 + 15,000 - 80,000 = 540,000. Prime cost = 540,000 + 310,000 + 45,000 = 895,000. Overheads = 186,000. Factory cost 1,081,000; adjusted for WIP (+28,000 - 34,000) gives cost of production 1,075,000, i.e. N43 per unit.

questions.stem:
The following is a summary of the cash transactions of Unity Youth Club for the year ended 31 December: cash in hand 1 January N42,000; subscriptions received N365,000; donations received N50,000; proceeds of annual dance N88,000; dance expenses N31,000; rent of hall N120,000; secretary's honorarium N60,000; purchase of equipment N150,000; stationery N18,000.
Additional information: (i) subscriptions owing at 31 December, N25,000; (ii) subscriptions received in advance for next year, included above, N10,000; (iii) rent owing, N20,000; (iv) equipment is to be depreciated at 10%. There were no subscriptions in arrears or in advance at the start of the year, and donations are treated as revenue.
(a) Prepare the receipts and payments account. [8 marks]
(b) Prepare the income and expenditure account. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: opening cash 42,000
2 marks: receipts: subscriptions 365,000, donations 50,000, dance 88,000
3 marks: payments: dance 31,000, rent 120,000, honorarium 60,000, equipment 150,000, stationery 18,000
2 marks: closing cash N166,000
3 marks: subscriptions income 365,000 + 25,000 - 10,000 = 380,000
1 mark: donations 50,000
2 marks: profit on dance 57,000
2 marks: rent 140,000
2 marks: depreciation 15,000, with honorarium 60,000 and stationery 18,000
2 marks: surplus N254,000
questions.explanation: Closing cash = 545,000 available (opening cash plus receipts) less 379,000 paid = 166,000. Income: subscriptions 380,000, donations 50,000, dance profit 57,000 = 487,000. Expenditure: rent 140,000, honorarium 60,000, stationery 18,000, depreciation 15,000 = 233,000. Excess of income over expenditure (surplus) = 254,000.
